title: observability: token-level KV cache metrics + dashboards + alert tuning
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes:
- Add token-level KV cache metrics (kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.misses, kv_cache.evictions, kv_cache.memory_bytes)
- New Grafana dashboards for token-level cost & latency breakdowns including KV hit/miss impact
- Tuned Prometheus alert rules to reduce noise and reflect observed SLOs
- Minor docs and example queries added
description:
Context: We need better observability around the KV cache so engineers can correlate token-level latency and cost with cache behavior. Current dashboards show aggregate cache hit rates but that hides token-length and model-variant effects which drove a recent incident (SUP-3245). This PR adds token-level KV metrics, expands tracing hooks to tag requests with KV outcomes, and ships Grafana dashboards and updated alert rules.

What this PR does (summary):
- Emit token-level KV metrics from the serving runtime: kv_cache.tokens_hitted_total, kv_cache.tokens_missed_total, kv_cache.tokens_evicted_total, kv_cache.memory_bytes. Metrics are emitted with labels: model, deployment, region, quantization_profile, sequence_bucket (e.g. 0-64,65-256,256+).
- Instrument tracing to add span attributes for kv_hit_ratio and kv_hot_lookups to make traces filterable by cache behavior.
- Add a new Grafana dashboard (observability/token-kv-cache-token-level.json) with panels: Token-level KV hit rate, Token-level latency breakdown (cache hit vs miss), Token-level cost delta, Per-model sequence bucket heatmap.
- Update Prometheus alerting rules: adjust thresholds and add cooldowns for kv_cache.low_hit_rate and kv_cache.memory_pressure; added a new alert kv_cache.sustained_miss_rate for 5m->30m windows to catch regressions without spamming on short spikes.
- Add docs and dashboard runbook snippets for debugging token-level cache issues.
- Add end-to-end tests and a small runtime simulator that validates metrics labels under varied sequence distributions.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime metrics and labels implemented
- [x] Tracing attributes added
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and templating added
- [x] Prometheus alert rules updated and unit-tested
- [x] Docs and runbook updated
- [x] Unit/integration tests added

Motivation: With increasing adoption of long-context prompts and new quantized model variants, cache behavior became a first-order factor in per-token latency and cost. This work gives operators the signals to correlate KV cache behavior directly with token-level performance and to tune batching/caching policies accordingly.

Notes on rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_token_kv_metrics` (off by default for older private installs). For Hosted and Dedicated rollout we enable behind a phased release and monitor metric cardinality for the first 48h to ensure we don't blow up Prometheus ingestion. Dashboard is read-only until rollout completes.

Related: ENG-3820 (batching improvements), SRE-159 (alert policy updates), SUP-3245 (incident driving change).

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a couple of comments on metric naming and cardinality. Can we collapse model_version -> model to avoid dimensional explosion?
Ava Thompson: Reply: dropped model_version label, kept model and quantization_profile; added sequence_bucket to control cardinality. Also added a sparseness test to the e2e simulator.
Priya Kapoor: Alert tuning looks better; suggest increasing cooldown for kv_cache.memory_pressure to 15m to avoid flapping during scheduled maintenance windows.
Ava Thompson: Applied change and added a short note in the runbook about scheduled maintenance windows and how to mute alerts.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after verifying dashboard panels render in dev Grafana and alerts fire in the test rule runner.
SRE team (thread): Please monitor prometheus ingestion rate closely after rollout; we rolled back once in a canary where cardinality jumped unexpectedly.

merge_info: Merged by squash (squash and merge) on 2026-02-26. Merge commit message: 'observability: token-level KV cache metrics, dashboards, and alert tuning (ENG-4821, SRE-159)'.
notes_metrics: New metrics added: kv_cache_tokens_hitted_total, kv_cache_tokens_missed_total, kv_cache_tokens_evicted_total, kv_cache_memory_bytes. Prometheus job: redwood-runtime/kv_cache. Labels: model, deployment, region, quantization_profile, sequence_bucket.
notes_alerts: Alert changes: kv_cache.low_hit_rate (now 5m avg < 0.6 for high-QPS deployments, 15m cooldown), kv_cache.memory_pressure (threshold updated with 15m cooldown), kv_cache.sustained_miss_rate (5m->30m window). Added silence recipes to runbook.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Enable in dev Canary (1 host) for 24h and observe prometheus cardinality and e2e traces. Phase 2: Gradual enable on Hosted and Dedicated 10%/50%/100% over 48h. Phase 3: Enable for Private installs via opt-in feature flag and include migration notes in release notes.
runbook_snippet: To investigate latency spikes correlated with tokens: 1) Open token-kv-cache Grafana dashboard, filter by model and sequence_bucket; 2) Check 'Token-level latency breakdown' and compare hit vs miss panels; 3) If miss rate is high, check kv_cache.memory_bytes and recent evictions; 4) Use traces tag kv_hit_ratio to inspect request spans and trace hot-lookup counts; 5) Consider increasing cache size or tuning batcher policy.
follow_up: Track prometheus ingestion rate metric for 72h after rollout (SLO target: <10% increase). If cardinality exceeds threshold, revert feature flag and iterate on sequence_bucket aggregation.
